operations.evidence: Guidance applies in England and covers private and social rented sectors after the 2025 extension.
Regulatory scope was not treated as a named-property condition.
Landlords must have installations inspected and tested by a qualified person at least every five years.
The interval was not treated as proof of continuous safety.
Landlords must obtain a report and provide it to tenants and councils when requested.
Report existence was separated from remedial-work completion.
Coverage generally requires only-or-main-residence occupation and rent.
Tenancy coverage was not inferred without legal occupancy evidence.
The guidance lists shared accommodation, long leases, halls, hostels, care settings and mobile-home exclusions.
No exclusion was assigned to a parcel without tenancy evidence.
Electrical standards are set by BS 7671, the 18th Edition Wiring Regulations.
A standards reference was not represented as installation compliance.
Installations include permanently connected equipment and specialist circuits such as solar PV and battery storage.
Equipment presence was not inferred for a parcel.
Inspection considers overload, shock, fire, defective work and earthing or bonding hazards.
The checklist was not treated as a defect finding.
The EICR gives results and the next inspection date.
No next date was inferred without the actual report.
C1 means danger present and risk of injury.
The definition was not used as evidence of a C1 defect at a property.
C2 means potentially dangerous.
C2 was not converted into a parcel probability.
C3 means improvement recommended and does not itself require remedial work for a satisfactory report.
C3 was represented as neither confirmed danger nor confirmed absence of risk.
FI means further investigation required without delay.
FI was not represented as a final defect or outcome.
Social landlords must check provided electrical equipment at least every five years.
The duty was not treated as evidence of equipment condition.
Local councils may impose penalties up to £40,000 for specified breaches.
The statutory ceiling was not treated as evidence of a breach or imposed penalty.
The wave35 electrical source-id prefix had no indexed repository match before publication.
Zero source roles were promoted to parcel evidence, candidate values or business rows.
15 source rows and 34 operation rows were prepared for line-by-line website visibility.
No second runner, queue replacement, runtime execution or business-data write was performed.
